questions.q: In this lab, why does `ChangeFreezeChecker` need to extend `AbstractAjaxProcessor` and have Client callable checked?
options: So the client script's GlideAjax call is allowed to reach `isDateInFreezeWindow` at all
Those settings are only needed for Business Rules, not Script Includes
To make the Script Include run faster
So `g_form.addInfoMessage` works correctly
questions.explain: Both are required before GlideAjax can call any method on a Script Include - without them, the client-side call would simply fail to reach the server method.

options: `_overlapsFreeze` doesn't exist until `isDateInFreezeWindow` runs
`isDateInFreezeWindow` has a plain public name; `_overlapsFreeze` has a leading underscore, which makes it unreachable from the client regardless of the Script Include's Client callable setting
Both methods are actually callable from the client
GlideAjax can only call methods that return a boolean, not a string
questions.explain: The underscore-prefix convention from Lesson 19 applies here: only non-underscore method names are valid sysparm_name targets.

questions.q: In the client script's `onChange` function, why does it check `if (!startDate || !endDate) { return; }` before making the GlideAjax call?
options: To avoid sending an incomplete date range to the server for a check that can't yet be meaningful
Because GlideAjax calls fail automatically if any parameter is empty
Because g_form.getValue() throws an error on an empty field
This check has no real purpose and could be removed
questions.explain: There's no point running the freeze check server-side until both dates are actually set - this guard avoids a wasted round trip.

questions.q: Where does the lab's `g_form.addInfoMessage()` call live, and why does that placement matter?
options: Immediately after `ga.getXMLAnswer(...)` is called, so it runs right away
Inside the `getXMLAnswer` callback function, because that's the only point where the server's real answer is guaranteed to be available
Inside the Script Include, since only server-side code can call g_form
It doesn't matter where it's placed, as long as it's somewhere in the function
questions.explain: As Lesson 20 covered, anything that depends on the GlideAjax answer must run inside the callback - placing it elsewhere would read an answer that isn't ready yet.

questions.q: The lab notes that if the freeze dates ever need to come from a real configuration table instead of two hardcoded strings, only `ChangeFreezeChecker` needs to change. Why is that true?
options: Because the client script never sees date logic directly - it only sends two date parameters and reads back a plain 'true'/'false' answer
Because the client script also hardcodes the same freeze dates as a backup
It isn't true - both files would need to change
Because GlideDateTime automatically syncs with the client script's variables
questions.explain: The client script's contract with the server is just two date parameters in, a true/false string out - all freeze-window logic is isolated inside the Script Include.
